# Paper results

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_paper_results.py from paper/reported_results.json and paper/sources.json. -->

CROSS-MORSE reports a different useful control regime across seven benchmarks: radius control on ogbn-arxiv and ogbn-proteins, receding-horizon control on Roman-empire, PascalVOC-SP and COCO-SP, a boundary radius result on Peptides-func, and return of the open-loop comparator on ogbn-products. The reported paired loss improvement reaches **0.00905 nats**, official-metric gains reach **0.65 percentage points**, and the six feedback deployments have **15–33% expected serial-work overhead** over their selected comparators.

These are **our reported measurements, transcribed from the submitted manuscript for comparison only**. The repository preserves their printed values and makes the numerical ledgers inspectable; the paper's run-derived tables and figures are built from completed run directories by `make paper` ([paper/README.md](../paper/README.md)). The separately bundled CPU lifecycle checks establish software behavior; they are not reruns of these benchmark experiments. Main abstract, p1; Table 1, p11; Table 2, p14.

The reported admission decisions are **descriptive on all seven benchmarks**. The three independent-graph benchmarks reused validation for confirmation and admission, so their reported bounds do not instantiate the independent-graph theorem. The single-graph benchmarks use dependent cores or official splits. This scope accompanies the measurements throughout this page. Main pp7,11; Supplementary Note S26, p31.

## 1. Paired test effects against the selected comparator

The estimand is `loss(qD) − loss(qC)`; negative loss differences favor deployment. `qC` is the selected open-loop comparator, and `E` is the retained ensemble size. Brackets below are the paper's **95% paired test intervals**, not ranges over configurations. CE and mean multilabel BCE are reported in nats. Official gains are percentage points, including the explicit conversion from native AP for Peptides.

| Dataset | qC | Reported qD | E | Loss | Paired loss difference [95% CI] | Metric gain [95% CI], pp |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ogbn-arxiv | fixed sequence | radius | 4 | CE | −0.00450 [−0.00750, −0.00150] | +0.07 [+0.01, +0.13] |
| ogbn-proteins | learned stop / fixed sequence† | radius | 4 | BCE | −0.00380 [−0.00680, −0.00080] | +0.11 [+0.03, +0.19] |
| ogbn-products | phase, boundaries 8/32 | qC returned | 2 | CE | 0 (identity) | 0 (identity) |
| Roman-empire | MPC-OL, H = 8 | MPC-RH | 4 | CE | −0.00572 [−0.00889, −0.00255] | +0.26 [+0.10, +0.42] |
| PascalVOC-SP | MPC-OL, H = 16 | MPC-RH | 8 | CE | −0.00842 [−0.01278, −0.00406] | +0.60 [+0.38, +0.82] |
| COCO-SP | MPC-OL, H = 16 | MPC-RH | 8 | CE | −0.00905 [−0.01268, −0.00542] | +0.65 [+0.42, +0.88] |
| Peptides-func | fixed sequence | radius | 4 | BCE | −0.00303 [−0.00474, −0.00132] | +0.58 [+0.09, +1.07] |

Source: main Table 1, p11. Peptides' native result is **+0.0058 AP [0.0009, 0.0107]**, equivalent to +0.58 [0.09, 1.07] AP percentage points. †The paper names proteins' comparator in two ways; the unavailable full selection record would identify the single executed rule (Table S35, R18, p23).

**Products is an informative comparator-return result.** Its supported improvement set is empty, so admission is not evaluated and `qD = qC` exactly. The zero effect is an execution identity, not an estimated improvement with a zero-width confidence interval. The state-destruction test has P = 0.42 against zero; equivalence within ±0.002 nats was not tested. Main Table 1; Table S14, p10.

## 2. Absolute official scores and what is not tabulated

`q0` denotes the upstream predictor, `qN` the nominal full-depth frozen plant, `qC` the selected comparator, and `qD` the deployment. Table S15 supplies the latter three official scores. Its full-depth plant row is **qN**; it is not a q0 measurement.

| Dataset | Official-score unit | q0 | qN | qC | qD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ogbn-arxiv | accuracy, % | not tabulated | 72.93 | 73.15 | 73.22 |
| ogbn-proteins | ROC-AUC, % | not tabulated | 87.02 | 87.15 | 87.26 |
| ogbn-products | accuracy, % | not tabulated | 87.59 | 87.74 | 87.74 |
| Roman-empire | accuracy, % | not tabulated | 91.76 | 92.37 | 92.63 |
| PascalVOC-SP | macro F1, % | not tabulated | 46.89 | 47.61 | 48.21 |
| COCO-SP | macro F1, % | not tabulated | 31.60 | 32.38 | 33.03 |
| Peptides-func | AP (native units) | not tabulated | 0.704 | 0.714 | 0.720 |

Source: Table S15, pp11–12. **Absolute test losses for q0/qN/qC/qD and q0's absolute official scores are not tabulated in these PDFs.** The paired effects above remain available. The reference plant-loss levels in Table S26 and depth-integrated losses in Table S16 are different quantities and are not substituted for missing absolute test losses.

Peptides has an explicitly retained cross-table discrepancy: Table S26 prints 0.7200 − 0.7140 = 0.0060 AP, whereas main Table 1 reports +0.0058 AP. The 0.0002 difference exceeds the 0.0001 maximum rounding discrepancy for two four-decimal scores. We retain the main paired estimate and the separately reported absolute scores; unrounded per-seed observations are not provided. Table S26 caption, p17.

Assurance cost is the separate configuration `Ccontroller + CqC`; it is not the attained maximum of the deployed rule. The 99th-percentile column is a resolvent-frequency **scenario model**, not an observed maximum or a hard cap.

Sources: main Table 2, p14; Table S23, p16; Table S44, p28. Percentages retain the paper's rounding from its more precise ledger. The exchange rate is derived from paired loss improvement divided by added expected work; its uncertainty comes from the paired effect interval.

The paper reports qualification increments of 1.4–2.3 GPU-hours. Table S41 separates component costs, while Table S35 retains an accounting-unit mismatch between the per-checkpoint, ensemble and search totals. Full-state sensing cannot explain the reported proteins/Pascal multipliers at every site: executed sketch width, sensing period and resolvent frequency are needed, and are not tabulated. ## 4. What confirmation and admission establish

The paper's confirmation map retains a route when its beneficial point estimate exceeds the practical margin and its zero-effect test passes Holm adjustment. Evidence against zero, evidence beyond the margin, and equivalence are distinct. Equality at a margin chooses the simpler route; a predecessor must remain in the selection-eligible set, otherwise the output is qC. Table S11, p8.

| Contrast | Effect, nats | 95% interval | Reported unit | Holm P vs zero | P vs practical margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| arxiv/state | +0.00574 | [+0.00312, +0.00836] | 32 buffered clusters | 0.0098 | 0.0026 |
| arxiv/radius | −0.00286 | [−0.00481, −0.00091] | 32 buffered clusters | 0.015 | 0.0858 |
| proteins/state | +0.00485 | [+0.00264, +0.00706] | 32 buffered clusters | 0.0098 | 0.0057 |
| proteins/radius | −0.00242 | [−0.00406, −0.00077] | 32 buffered clusters | 0.015 | 0.1365 |
| products/state | +0.00036 | [−0.00064, +0.00136] | 64 buffered clusters | 0.42 | — |
| Roman/RH | −0.00649 | [−0.01007, −0.00291] | 10 official splits | 0.015 | 0.007 |
| Pascal/RH | −0.00902 | [−0.01355, −0.00449] | 1428 validation graphs (= admission split under the submitted protocol) | < 0.001 | 0.0012 |
| COCO/RH | −0.00962 | [−0.01372, −0.00552] | 5000 validation graphs (= admission split under the submitted protocol) | < 0.001 | < 0.001 |
| Peptides/radius | −0.00172 | [−0.00316, −0.00028] | 2331 validation graphs (= admission split under the submitted protocol) | 0.036 | 0.3823 |

Source: Table S14, p10, one reported Holm family of nine contrasts. State destruction changes controller observations, preserving the plant state. Arxiv/proteins radius contrasts pass the paper's point-estimate rule, while their one-sided tests do not establish improvement beyond 0.0015 nats. Peptides is similarly a boundary result. Its five-fold label count is not the fraction of test graphs receiving feedback.

For the three independent-graph datasets, the reported admission arithmetic is:

| Dataset | Graphs J | Clipped mean | Variance | Bound penalty | Ua | Required margin | Reported status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PascalVOC-SP | 1428 | −0.00836 | 0.000214 | 0.002578 | −0.005782 | 0.003 | descriptive pass |
| COCO-SP | 5000 | −0.00901 | 0.000263 | 0.001088 | −0.007922 | 0.003 | descriptive pass |
| Peptides-func | 2331 | −0.00311 | 0.000126 | 0.001566 | −0.001544 | 0.0015 | descriptive pass |

The clip is B = 0.10 and δa = 0.025; all three rows report a passing official-metric gate. The theorem's target is expected clipped paired loss, not unrestricted unclipped harm. These are moments for a fixed deployed ensemble. The main test intervals also resample optimization seeds, so their larger widths describe a different uncertainty population. Fixed-moment sensitivity at B = 0.20 makes Peptides fail the admission inequality; this calculation does not re-clip raw observations. Table S13, pp9–10; Note S24, p31.

**Separated-data sensitivity is not a rerun.** Table S14b rescales standard errors at fixed effects to the registered confirmation sizes 850/11,329/1,087. Its model gives label-retention probabilities 0.85, >0.99 and 0.36 for Pascal, COCO and Peptides. Under the displayed Peptides sensitivity outcome the radius label fails and one-step is outside Qs, so the map returns qC with exactly zero effect and no admission step. These hypothetical statistics neither replace the reported radius measurement nor repair earlier validation reuse. Table S14b, pp10–11; Note S26, p31.

## 5. Counterfactuals and stronger comparators

The paper reports initial-input schedule prediction (E3), distillation (E4), replanning without new observations (E5), and budget-aware execution (E6). The central arm outcomes below use **millinats relative to qC**. Their configuration ranges remain in the full registry; they are not confidence intervals.

| Dataset | Reported feedback | E3 predictor | E4 distilled | E5 no observation | E6 budget aware | E6 overhead |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ogbn-arxiv | -4.5 | -1.6 | -1.4 | -1.3 | -4.4 | 6% |
| ogbn-proteins | -3.8 | -1.3 | -1.2 | -1.1 | -3.7 | 7% |
| Roman-empire | -5.7 | -1.4 | -1.3 | -0.5 | -5.5 | 11% |
| PascalVOC-SP | -8.4 | -2.1 | -1.9 | -0.7 | -8.1 | 10% |
| COCO-SP | -9.1 | -2.3 | -2.0 | -0.7 | -8.7 | 10% |
| Peptides-func | -3.0 | -1.1 | -1.0 | -0.8 | -2.9 | 9% |

Source: Tables S46–S46b, p29. The common-ceiling protocol is specified, but arm-level paired intervals, adjusted P values, actual-work observations and budget mismatches are not tabulated. The point outcomes can be reported without inventing those missing statistics. Tables S42/S47 are analytical power and decision-boundary calculations, not observed rejection frequencies. These auxiliary arms and external architecture reruns are reported evidence; they are outside the packaged nine-route runner. [Claims ledger](../paper/claims_ledger.md); [implementation differences](../paper/KNOWN_DIFFERENCES.md).

Additional reported comparisons include native-site versus inserted-site feedback (Table S45), matched reruns of external architectures (Tables S15/S15b), and the extended comparator ensemble grid E = 1,2,4,8,12,16,20 (Tables S26/S26b). The extra checkpoints in the extended grid are separately costed diagnostics. Noninteger cost-matched ensemble sizes and ensemble-spend crossovers are analytical sensitivity models, not executable ensembles or properties established for a learned predictor.

## 6. Decision rules and qualifications retained in this registry

| Issue | How the public record handles it | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Registered selector versus reported selections | Keep the reported MPC-RH deployments. Eq.19 with εeq=0.002 on upper limits selects radius on three representative rows; it matches four of seven. The full executed trace is needed to identify the actual rule. | S12c p9, main p11 |
| Support statistics | Preserve current reported counts, propensities and qualified fractions; corrected per-cell ESS/max-weight summaries are explicitly missing. Withdrawn inconsistent dataset-level pairs are not recycled as evidence. | S7 p5, main pp17–18 |
| Headroom | A label-informed oracle measures available opportunity. Its confidence limit is not an attained task gain or an executable label-free policy. | Main Proposition4 p7, S30 p20 |
| Factorial evidence | Arxiv cell010 changes predictions at zero activity and is excluded from an additivity interpretation. Pascal's eight decision-capable cells use a different factor definition. Paired interactions need joint covariance. | S16–S16b pp12–13, S17d p38 |
| Conditional guarantees | Max-t coverage and selective-sensing invariance are assumptions/audit targets. Checking formulas or software does not establish those events for all future inputs. | Main pp6–9, [method scope](METHOD_OVERVIEW.md) |

## 7. Trace a value or attach the underlying run

The single numeric registry is [paper/reported_results.json](../paper/reported_results.json). [paper/sources.json](../paper/sources.json) maps every numerical group to a PDF, exact SHA-256, page and evidence type. The broader [table rendering](../paper/REPORTED_RESULTS.md) and [CSV summary](../results/paper_summary.csv) are generated views. A blank CSV value means not tabulated, never an inferred zero.

```bash
python -B scripts/render_paper_results.py --check
python -B scripts/render_reported_results.py --check
python -B scripts/check_paper_constants.py
```

These commands verify the recorded source identities, provenance coverage, generated views and registered arithmetic. They do not rerun a benchmark. To validate a completed run, replay its sealed statistics, re-execute checkpoints, or attach a manuscript-run binding, follow [Results and replay](RESULTS.md) and the [reviewer guide](REVIEWER_GUIDE.md). Our paper-run prediction/checkpoint archives enter the repository through the run-archive contract ([RUN_ARCHIVES.md](RUN_ARCHIVES.md)); the binding templates do not assert identities for archives that are not yet ingested.
